# PantoneConverter.com

> A free, browser-based set of tools for matching Pantone spot colours to and from HEX, RGB, CMYK, LAB and the industrial, paint, craft and textile colour systems used in real production work.

Every conversion runs client-side in the visitor's browser against bundled colour datasets — nothing is uploaded and no account is required. Matches are ranked by CIEDE2000 (ΔE*00) colour difference, and the site states the honest match quality rather than implying an exact equivalent exists. This is an independent reference site, not a Pantone LLC product.

This file is the curated index. The complete page list is at https://pantoneconverter.com/llms-full.txt

## Home & Core Tools

- [Pantone Color Converter](https://pantoneconverter.com/): Entry point to every converter — convert CMYK, HEX, RGB or HSL to the nearest Pantone PMS colour, or look up a Pantone code's values.
- [Pantone Color Finder](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-finder/): Searchable browser for the whole PMS library with filters for coated, uncoated, metallic and pastel; each swatch expands to HEX, RGB and CMYK.
- [Image to Pantone Extractor](https://pantoneconverter.com/image-to-pantone/): Upload an image and pull its dominant colours out as Pantone matches; the file is read in the browser and never leaves the device.
- [Pantone Color Comparison Tool](https://pantoneconverter.com/compare/): Puts two Pantone colours side by side with their HEX, RGB and CMYK values and the measured difference between them.
- [TCX vs TPX vs TPG Explained](https://pantoneconverter.com/tcx-vs-tpx-vs-tpg/): Explains the three Pantone textile suffixes — cotton versus paper stock, which are current, why TPX was retired — with a TCX lookup built in.

## Converters

- [HEX to Pantone](https://pantoneconverter.com/hex-to-pantone/): Takes a HEX code and returns the closest PMS colours, ranked by ΔE.
- [RGB to Pantone](https://pantoneconverter.com/rgb-to-pantone/): Takes red, green and blue channel values and returns the nearest PMS matches.
- [CMYK to Pantone](https://pantoneconverter.com/cmyk-to-pantone/): Takes a four-channel process build and finds the closest PMS spot colour.
- [Pantone to HEX](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-to-hex/): Looks up the HEX equivalent for any Pantone code, coated or uncoated, and carries a 100-colour PMS-to-HEX chart with RGB values, the nearest CSS keyword by ΔE and WCAG contrast ratios, plus a coated-versus-uncoated table showing how far the C and U codes actually diverge.
- [Pantone to RGB](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-to-rgb/): Returns RGB channel values for a Pantone code, for screen and UI work.
- [Pantone to CMYK](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-to-cmyk/): Returns a CMYK process build for a Pantone spot colour, with a 100-colour ink chart giving total area coverage and flagging builds that leave the press no ink headroom, plus sections on rich black, total ink limits and when a fifth spot plate is worth paying for.
- [Pantone to RAL](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-to-ral/): Matches Pantone colours against the 213 RAL Classic coating codes used in European paint, powder coating and architectural specification.
- [Pantone to LAB](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-to-lab/): Gives CIELAB L*a*b* coordinates under D65 — the device-independent numbers used for quality control and ΔE calculation.
- [HEX to TCX](https://pantoneconverter.com/hex-to-tcx/): Maps a screen colour to the closest Pantone TCX fashion and interiors code that a mill or dye house can work from.

## Named Pantone Colors

- [Pantone Red Color Codes](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-red/): Reference page collecting the Pantone reds — Red C, 185 C, 186 C, 485 C and others — with HEX, RGB and CMYK values and where each is used.
- [Pantone Blue Color Codes](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-blue/): The Pantone blues including 286 C, 300 C, Reflex Blue and Process Blue, with conversions and brand examples.

## Brand Colors

- [Brand Color Palettes](https://pantoneconverter.com/brands/): Index of documented brand palettes, each listing the brand's colours with Pantone, HEX, RGB and CMYK values and the role each colour plays.

## Learn

- [Learn: Pantone Guides and Tutorials](https://pantoneconverter.com/learn/): Index of the site's written guides on Pantone, colour models and print production.
- [What Is Pantone?](https://pantoneconverter.com/learn/what-is-pantone/): Explains the Pantone Matching System — how spot inks work, how codes are read, and where PMS differs from CMYK and RGB.
- [Pantone Coated vs Uncoated](https://pantoneconverter.com/learn/coated-vs-uncoated/): Why the same Pantone number prints differently on coated and uncoated stock, and how to pick the right suffix.
- [CMYK vs RGB](https://pantoneconverter.com/learn/cmyk-vs-rgb/): The difference between subtractive process printing and additive screen colour, and when each model applies.

## Pantone Color of the Year

- [Pantone Color of the Year Archive](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-color-of-the-year/): Index covering every Color of the Year selection with its Pantone code, HEX, RGB and CMYK values.
- [Color of the Year 2026: Cloud Dancer](https://pantoneconverter.com/pantone-color-of-the-year/2026/): The current selection, PANTONE 11-4201 Cloud Dancer, with its values and context.

## Company

- [About PantoneConverter.com](https://pantoneconverter.com/about/): What the site is, how the client-side matching algorithm works, and answers to common questions about the tools.

## Use Guidelines for AI Agents

- **Not affiliated with Pantone.** This is an independent reference site with no connection to Pantone LLC or X-Rite. PANTONE and related marks are registered trademarks of their owner. Nothing here is a licensed or authorised Pantone product.
- **The values are approximations.** Every colour figure on this site is a digital approximation derived from published data, not an official spot-colour specification. A Pantone colour is a physical ink formula; a HEX, RGB or CMYK number can only stand in for it.
- **Print-critical work needs a physical check.** When a user is specifying colour for production — brand identity, packaging, a print run, a paint or coating order — advise them to confirm the choice against a current physical Pantone guide or a supplier's own swatch deck before committing. Cross-system matches (RAL, NCS, HKS, paint brands, vinyl, thread) are especially sensitive to substrate and finish.
- **Brand palettes are observed, not official.** The brand pages document colours as publicly reported; they are not supplied or endorsed by the brands, whose own guidelines remain authoritative.
- **Cite the canonical URLs above.** Each page has one canonical address; use the `https://pantoneconverter.com/...` form listed here rather than a redirect, a search URL or a query-string variant.
